Triggers.value: Talk about people loosing loved ones

Maladaptive Strategies.value: I dwell on how the event could have been prevented
I clean or organise things repeatedly to feel in control
I try to erase the memory of the event

Memory.value: Sometimes I can recall what happened but feel completely numb, as if it happened to a stranger
The memory feels like it is happening right now rather than something that is over
The memory is so extreme it is hard to believe it actually happened to me

Negative Appraisals.value: My beliefs about how the world works have been completely destroyed
The world is a dangerous place
What happened to me was deeply unfair and nothing has been done about it

issues.item: Sexual Objectification: Being looked at sexually
issues.explanation: For a 78-year-old woman whose index trauma is a natural disaster, this trigger is clinically hard to reconcile with the rest of the profile. The other triggers, appraisals, memory items, and strategies all fit disaster-related loss/danger themes, but 'being looked at sexually' implies a sexual-threat/sexual-trauma context that is not represented anywhere else in the formulation or item set. This is more than unusual; it introduces a qualitatively different trauma meaning network without supporting items in Threat, Memory, Appraisals, or Strategies.

vignette: It's been nearly a decade since the hurricane ravaged her small coastal town, yet for Emilia, the memories still linger like an open wound. She recalls the sound of the front door bursting open, the howling wind, and the feeling of utter chaos as her home was torn apart. The trauma has left an indelible mark on her life, one that she struggles to shake off even in the quiet moments. The slightest creak of a door opening or slamming can transport Emilia back to that fateful day. Her heart racing, she is convinced that disaster is lurking around every corner, waiting to strike again. The world, once a predictable and safe place, has become a treacherous landscape where anything can happen without warning. Conversations about loss and tragedy only serve to reinforce this notion, making her dwell on the what-ifs and the could-haves. Even the smell of alcohol, a common scent in the aftermath of the storm, is enough to trigger a cascade of memories she would rather forget. Emilia's attempts to regain control over her life have led her down a path of rumination and compulsive behavior. She spends hours poring over news articles and documentaries about natural disasters, convinced that if only she had been better prepared, things might have turned out differently. Her graphic design work, once a source of joy and creativity, has become a chore as she becomes fixated on reorganizing her workspace and perfecting every detail. This excessive attention to detail is an attempt to impose order on a world that feels increasingly capricious. Despite the passing years, Emilia's memories of the hurricane remain vivid yet strangely disconnected from her emotions. There are times when she can recall the events with eerie clarity, only to feel as though she is observing someone else's life. The story of what happened feels almost surreal, like a narrative she has constructed rather than lived through. And yet, in other moments, the memory feels agonizingly present, as if the storm could sweep back into her life at any moment. Emilia's sense of injustice and outrage still simmers just below the surface. The lack of accountability for the disaster's aftermath and the perceived failure of authorities to prevent such tragedies only serves to fuel her feelings of resentment and powerlessness. This perception of a world that is fundamentally unfair has become a self-reinforcing cycle, driving her maladaptive strategies and further entrenching her negative appraisals. As Emilia navigates this complex web of emotions and memories, she finds herself increasingly withdrawn from the world around her. Her relationships with loved ones suffer as she becomes more isolated, fearful of being overwhelmed by her own thoughts and emotions. It is only when she is confronted with the possibility of losing her husband to illness that Emilia realizes she can no longer continue down this path alone. With a sense of trepidation, she begins to seek help, hoping to break free from the cycle of fear, rumination, and avoidance that has come to define her life. Emilia's eyes well up with tears as she finally acknowledges the depth of her pain and the overwhelming sense of injustice that still gnaws at her soul. It is this moment of raw vulnerability that marks the beginning of her journey towards healing, one that will require her to confront the shattered remains of her old self and slowly rebuild a new narrative - one where trauma no longer defines her every waking moment.
